question: Who was the first woman of Indian descent to go to space? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Kalpana Chawla
Nalini Ramarajan
Shawna Pandya
Sunita Willianms
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kalpana Chawla

Explanation:
Kalpana Chawla was the first woman of Indian descent to go to space. She flew as an astronaut on the STS-87 mission in 1997. She was a naturalized U.S. citizen but was born in India. She worked as a NASA astronaut and became the first Indian-born woman to travel to space. Later, Sunita Williams also went to space, but Kalpana Chawla was the first. Tragically, she died in the Columbia space shuttle disaster in 2003. Her achievement inspired many women in India and around the world to pursue careers in space exploration.

question: In which year did the Pulwama terror attack take place? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 2019
2017
2016
2018
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2019

Explanation:
The Pulwama terror attack took place on 14 February 2019 in the Pulwama district of Jammu and Kashmir. In this attack, a suicide bomber targeted a convoy of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), killing 40 soldiers. The responsibility was claimed by Pakistan-based terrorist organization Jaish-e-Mohammed. Following the attack, India conducted the Balakot airstrike (26 February 2019), destroying terrorist camps in Pakistan. This attack marked a significant turning point in India-Pakistan relations.

question: In which state is the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, located? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Andhra Pradesh
Kerala
Tamil Nadu
Karnataka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Andhra Pradesh

Explanation:
The Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) is located at Sriharikota, which lies in the Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh, along the Bay of Bengal coast. It is the primary launch center of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). From here, launch vehicles like PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3 are launched. The center is strategically located near the equator, providing an advantage for rocket launches. It was originally known as Sriharikota Range (SHAR) and was renamed in 2002 after former ISRO chairman Satish Dhawan. The facility includes multiple launch pads, a vehicle assembly building, and a mission control center.

☛ After whom is SDSC named? → Satish Dhawan

question: In which city was the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) signed between India and Pakistan, in 1960? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Calcutta
Lahore
Bombay
Karachi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Karachi

Explanation:
The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) was signed on September 19, 1960, between then Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistani President Ayub Khan. The treaty was mediated by the World Bank. The signing ceremony took place in the Pakistani city of Karachi. This treaty governs the sharing of water from the Indus River system, allocating the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India and the three western rivers (Indus, Chenab, Jhelum) to Pakistan. It is considered one of the most successful water-sharing treaties in the world and forms the basis for resolving water disputes between the two countries.

☛ Who mediated the treaty? → World Bank
☛ Which rivers were allocated to India? → Ravi, Beas, Sutlej

☛ In which city was it signed? → Karachi

question: Who is regarded as the Father of the Indian Nuclear Program? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/01/2021) Shift 2)

question: In the UN Security Council there are: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/01/2021) Shift 2)

question: On which day is World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought observed? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 22nd May
5th June
22nd April
17th June
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 17th June

Explanation:
The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed annually on 17 June. It was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1994, the same year the UNCCD (United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification) was adopted. The day aims to promote awareness of desertification and drought issues and encourage action to prevent land degradation. It is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 15 (Life on Land), which focuses on protecting, restoring, and promoting sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems. In India, desertification is a serious problem affecting about 30% of the country's land area.
